To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have localized and identified by biochemical means five different integral membrane proteins of rat hepatocytes, and that we have demonstrated the suitability of two of these as domain-specific markers for the separation of plasma membrane subfractions.

we have identified five rat hepatocytes plasma membrane antigens using a combination of immunological and morphological techniques and localized three of these to specific domains of the intact plasma membrane.

five monoclonal antibodies were raised against rat hepatocyte plasma membranes, and that these antibodies localized and identified five different plasma membrane proteins, one of which was found in all three domains and four of which were restricted to one domain each.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of monoclonal antibodies to identify plasma membrane proteins and to characterize their domain specificities.
the use of hybridoma technology to identify, localize, and purify rat plasma membrane proteins.
the development of new tools that will allow us to study the structure and function of specific domains of the plasma membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these five proteins represent a subset of the total plasma membrane protein population and that they are all hepatocyte specific.
the antigens HA 4, HA 16, and HA 21 were localized to the bile canalical surface, HA 116 was localized to both the lateral and sinusodial surfaces, and CE 9 was localized to the lateral surface.
these antigens are integral membrane proteins that are localized in the sinusoidal, lateral, or bile canalicular domains of the plasma membrane of hepatocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the monoclonal antibodies described in these two papers are useful for the identification of specific plasma membrane proteins, and that they are also useful for monitoring the purification of membrane fractions.
we have identified and localized five new rat hepatocyte plasma membranes.
these five antigens are integral membrane proteins that can be used as endogenous domain-specific markers for the three recognizable surface domains on the hepatocyte.
The main takeaway from our work is that
monoclonal antibodies can be used to identify and localize membrane proteins that are present in only one domain of the hepatocyte surface and that are not easily detectable by other means.

the use of monoclonal antibodies in combination with morphologic methods provides a useful approach for identifying plasma membrane proteins in a variety of cell types, and that this approach can provide important clues about the function of those proteins.
the use of monoclonal antibodies in conjunction with morphological and subcellular fractionation methods can be used to localize plasma membrane proteins and to identify them.
